article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Las Vegas Lemon Skunk × OG Kush × Haze
Breeder: Nirvana Seeds
THC Content: 16–19%
CBD Content: Low, around 0.1–1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, lime, pineapple, citrus, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 550–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,000 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Lemon OG Haze approaches citrus cannabis from a distinctly old-school direction. Instead of tasting like lemon candy layered over dessert genetics, the cultivar combines the brightness of fresh lemon peel with Haze florals, OG earthiness, tropical fruit, and a sharper herbal edge. The effect follows a similarly energetic path. Mental stimulation tends to arrive quickly, often bringing alertness, motivation, and an increasingly animated mood before a gentler physical calm develops underneath.

Nirvana Seeds created this sativa-dominant hybrid from Las Vegas Lemon Skunk, OG Kush, and Haze #1, three genetic influences with very different strengths. Their intersection produced a marijuana plant capable of substantial yields, vigorous vertical growth, abundant resin, and an unmistakable citrus-heavy terpene profile. For growers with enough height and patience to manage its sativa tendencies, Lemon OG Haze can be considerably more rewarding than its moderate THC percentage initially suggests.
Genetics and Lineage

Nirvana Seeds lists the original photoperiod Lemon OG Haze genetics as Las Vegas Lemon Skunk × OG Kush × Haze #1. Las Vegas Lemon Skunk provides much of the sharp citrus identity. Lemon Skunk lines are associated with classic Skunk genetics selected for unusually strong lemon aromas, energetic effects, vigorous branching, and pungent flower. The Las Vegas selection intensifies that bright citrus character, contributing the lemon-peel fragrance that becomes immediately recognizable in mature Lemon OG Haze flowers.

OG Kush brings a very different group of traits. Its dense resin production, earthy Kush character, fuel-like pungency, and physically relaxing effects help provide weight beneath the brighter Skunk and Haze influences. OG genetics can also add structural strength and complexity to a terpene profile that might otherwise lean entirely toward citrus. Haze #1 supplies the strongest sativa influence in the pedigree. Traditional Haze genetics are associated with narrow leaves, extended stretch, cerebral effects, incense-like aromatics, and longer flowering times. Those characteristics remain visible in Lemon OG Haze, particularly in its tall structure, elongated branching, mental intensity, and preference for warm growing environments.

The three-part pedigree explains why the cultivar rarely feels like a simple lemon strain. Las Vegas Lemon Skunk drives the citrus, OG Kush adds resin and an earthy foundation, and Haze contributes the expansive cerebral quality. Nirvana’s selection emphasizes sativa-dominant growth while retaining enough OG influence to produce substantial flower weight. The finished plant therefore sits between classic Haze architecture and modern commercial productivity rather than behaving like an especially lanky pure sativa.
Effects and Experience

The onset can be remarkably quick. A few inhalations are often enough for the cerebral side to become noticeable, beginning with heightened awareness and a brighter, more animated train of thought. Mundane activities may suddenly seem easier to engage with, while music, conversation, gaming, creative hobbies, or outdoor activities can become more immersive. Rather than immediately relaxing the consumer into stillness, this hybrid tends to push attention outward. That quality makes it better suited to daytime or early evening than to the final hour before bed.

As the high develops, the energetic character becomes more complex. Mental activity remains prominent, but the OG Kush influence introduces enough body relaxation to prevent the experience from feeling completely sharp or restless for many consumers. A comfortable physical undertone can emerge beneath the Haze-driven stimulation, producing a state that combines alertness with a degree of bodily ease. At moderate doses, that balance can be useful for social occasions, creative work, long walks, household projects, or other situations where remaining engaged is part of the goal.

Increasing the dose changes the experience considerably. The cerebral intensity can become powerful enough to feel almost psychedelic for people with limited tolerance, and excessive consumption may cause racing thoughts, nervousness, dizziness, or temporary paranoia. The strain therefore rewards moderation despite THC levels that look relatively restrained beside today’s highest-testing weed. Experienced consumers may find the effects clear and productive, whereas THC-sensitive individuals should begin slowly and evaluate the initial cerebral response before consuming more.
Medical Benefits

Lemon OG Haze may appeal to medical marijuana consumers whose symptoms interfere with daytime motivation rather than those primarily seeking sedation. The uplifting mental character can be relevant for people dealing with low mood, stress, or fatigue, particularly when heavy indica strains create too much drowsiness. THC influences several neurological systems associated with mood, reward, pain perception, and appetite, although the response to inhaled cannabis varies substantially from one patient to another.

Physical discomfort may also become less intrusive once the initial cerebral phase settles. OG Kush ancestry gives the cultivar a relaxing component that can complement its mental effects without immediately creating couch-lock. Some patients may therefore prefer it for mild aches or tension during periods when they still need to remain active. Caryophyllene is another notable component of the chemical profile because it interacts with CB2 receptors, though the presence of a particular terpene does not guarantee a predictable medical outcome.

Fatigue is one of the situations in which this strain’s character is particularly distinctive. Haze and Lemon Skunk influences often produce an alert, energetic experience, making the cultivar substantially different from marijuana varieties chosen primarily for sleep. That same stimulation can become counterproductive for people prone to anxiety, however. Patients sensitive to THC-induced nervousness should use conservative amounts, and anyone taking medications or treating a significant medical condition should consider professional medical guidance rather than relying solely on strain descriptions .
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Lemon dominates the first impression, but it does not stand alone. Opening properly cured flower can release something closer to freshly cut lemon rind and lemongrass than sweet lemonade. Lime, herbs, earth, and a faint pungent note develop beneath the citrus, while breaking apart the buds can uncover sweeter floral and tropical aromas. Pineapple is particularly noticeable in some examples and gives the bouquet a softer fruit component that contrasts with the sharper lemon.

Limonene plays an obvious role in the citrus presentation, but Nirvana identifies caryophyllene and myrcene among the cultivar’s other dominant terpenes. Caryophyllene contributes dry pepper, spice, and a slightly musky quality. Myrcene introduces herbal, earthy, and tropical dimensions that help bridge the lemon and pineapple characteristics. Together, these compounds keep the aroma from becoming one-dimensional. Growing conditions and phenotype still matter greatly; one harvest may smell overwhelmingly of citrus peel, while another can lean further toward herbs, spice, tropical fruit, and OG-like earth.

The flavor follows a recognizable sequence. Sharp lemon often appears immediately on inhalation, followed by lime and a mild tropical sweetness. Pineapple becomes clearer through slower vaporization, while combustion tends to emphasize spice and earth on the exhale. The finish can remain distinctly citrusy on the palate long after the smoke or vapor has cleared. Careful drying is important because excessive temperatures can strip away the more volatile lemon compounds, leaving behind a flatter herbal taste that fails to represent the genetics properly.
Growing Information

Lemon OG Haze grows with obvious sativa influence. Plants develop rapidly during vegetative growth, producing long, thin side branches, narrow serrated leaves, and comparatively wide internodal spacing. Nirvana reports mature heights around 150–180 centimeters indoors or under controlled conditions, while unrestricted outdoor plants in warm climates can approach roughly two meters. Stretch can become substantial after the flowering cycle begins, making early training especially important in tents or rooms with limited vertical space.

Topping, tying, and Screen of Green techniques work particularly well because the flexible branches can be spread horizontally before they become heavily loaded with flowers. Pruning lower growth before flowering allows the plant to direct more energy toward productive upper sites while improving airflow through what can eventually become a large canopy. The cultivar is considered a strong feeder and responds well to intense light when root health and environmental conditions are stable. Heavy feeding should still be approached gradually; genetic tolerance does not eliminate the possibility of nutrient burn or salt accumulation.

Indoor flowering usually requires nine to eleven weeks, with roughly 70 days being common and slower phenotypes sometimes needing close to 77 days. That extra patience can pay off in yield. Nirvana lists approximately 550–650 grams per square meter under good indoor conditions, placing Lemon OG Haze firmly among its high-producing cultivars. Long branches can become top-heavy late in bloom, so stakes, netting, or other support should be installed before flower weight begins pulling branches downward.

Outdoor cultivation is particularly attractive in hot, sunny regions with long seasons. The plant handles heat, wind, and periods of dry weather relatively well, although regular irrigation remains essential for maximum production. Nirvana recommends a late-October harvest in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Plants started early in the season with generous root space may produce as much as approximately 1,000 grams each under exceptional conditions. Such figures represent genetic potential rather than a guaranteed harvest; latitude, sunlight, soil volume, weather, nutrition, irrigation, plant training, and pest pressure determine actual production.

Resin output deserves attention as well. Flowers develop an abundant trichome layer, and the extensive sugar leaf surrounding productive branches can provide useful extraction material. Growers making dry sift , water hash , or other concentrates may appreciate the combination of strong resin production and citrus-dominant aromatics. Because the plant’s greatest strengths are yield and terpene intensity, allowing adequate flower development and performing a slow, controlled cure generally produces better results than rushing the harvest.
FAQ
Is Lemon OG Haze an indica or sativa?

Lemon OG Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Nirvana Seeds bred the strain from Las Vegas Lemon Skunk, OG Kush, and Haze #1. Its tall structure, narrow leaves, strong flowering stretch, energetic effects, and longer bloom period reflect the sativa side of the lineage, while OG Kush contributes physical relaxation and additional flower density.
What is the THC level of Lemon OG Haze?

The Nirvana Seeds version is generally listed at approximately 16–19% THC. That puts it below many modern strains marketed primarily around extreme potency, but its fast cerebral onset can still feel powerful. Individual flower batches may vary depending on phenotype, cultivation, maturity, curing, and laboratory testing methods.
What does Lemon OG Haze taste like?

Sharp lemon and lime dominate the flavor, followed by pineapple, herbs, mild earth, and peppery spice. Properly cured flower can resemble fresh lemon peel or lemongrass rather than artificial lemon candy. Limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene are major contributors to the aromatic profile.
How long does Lemon OG Haze take to flower?

Indoor flowering usually takes approximately nine to eleven weeks, with many plants finishing around 70 days. Some phenotypes may require closer to 77 days. Outdoors, Nirvana places harvest toward the end of October in warm Northern Hemisphere climates, so growers in regions with short or wet autumns need to account for the relatively late finish.
Is Lemon OG Haze difficult to grow?

The cultivar is moderately difficult primarily because of its height, heavy feeding, flowering stretch, and large final flower mass. Experienced growers who train the canopy early can achieve very high yields. SCROG, topping, tying, pruning, strong lighting, and branch support are particularly useful. Outdoors, sufficient space and a warm, sunny season simplify cultivation considerably.
Final Thoughts on Lemon OG Haze

Lemon OG Haze succeeds because each part of its pedigree remains recognizable without overwhelming the others. Las Vegas Lemon Skunk supplies the aggressive citrus, Haze #1 creates the energetic cerebral character and lanky structure, while OG Kush adds resin, physical relaxation, and an earthy foundation. The combination results in marijuana that feels distinctly sativa-driven without becoming thin, weak, or commercially impractical.

Growers receive equally compelling traits. The plant can stretch dramatically, demands training, and asks for more patience than a quick-finishing indica, yet those requirements are balanced by exceptional productivity and abundant resin. Indoor harvests can reach impressive levels under a properly managed canopy, while outdoor specimens have the potential to become enormous in sunny climates. For consumers, the reward is a focused, uplifting experience accompanied by one of the more natural lemon profiles found in cannabis—sharp citrus peel, lime, pineapple, herbs, and spice rather than simple sweetness. Lemon OG Haze remains an excellent choice for anyone seeking energetic weed with genuine Haze character, substantial yield potential, and a terpene profile that earns the lemon name.
